card.title: ROYAL FUSILIERS

card.flavorText: The Royal Fusiliers (City of London Regiment) was a British Army infantry regiment with a distinguished history dating back to 1685. During WWII, its battalions served across multiple theaters, demonstrating versatility and resilience. The 1st Battalion, initially stationed in India, was deployed to Egypt in 1939. It participated in the East African Campaign in Abyssinia and later in Syria, where it was captured in 1941. After reformation in Palestine, the battalion served in Iraq and subsequently in Italy, contributing to the Allied efforts in the Mediterranean. The 2nd Battalion was part of the British Expeditionary Force in France in 1939. Following the retreat to Dunkirk, it was evacuated to the UK and later saw action in North Africa and Italy, in particular in the Battle of Monte Cassino and operations along the Gothic Line. The 8th and 9th Battalions, Territorial Army units, were involved in the North African Campaign and the Italian Campaign. They participated in the Salerno landings, the crossing of the Volturno River, and the Battle of Monte Cassino. Both battalions also fought at Anzio and advanced through the Gothic Line. While some battalions remained in the UK for home defense and training, the Royal Fusiliers active units played significant roles in key operations across Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East during WWII.
